---
title: "Running the workflows"
subtitle: "The five workflows, their runners, and the flags that matter"
---

The five root Snakefiles define the workflows. Invoke simulation through
`scripts/simulate_system.py` or the all-workflow runner, which validate the
operation and targets before launching Snakemake once. Direct Snakemake
commands remain supported for the other workflows.

| Entry point | id | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `analyze_climate.smk` | wf0 | The basin's historical climate — **model-free** |
| `build_model.smk` | wf1 | Builds the Wflow-SBM model, runs it on historical forcing |
| `analyze_projections.smk` | wf2 | CMIP6 change factors — a plausibility overlay |
| `generate_scenarios.smk` | wf3 | Publish a reusable scenario collection |
| `simulate_system.smk` via `scripts/simulate_system.py` | wf4 | Simulate a collection or reduce retained responses |

The convenience order is analyze_climate → generate_scenarios → build_model
→ simulate_system → analyze_projections. Generation and model construction are
independent prerequisites of simulation. WF0 is optional; run it first or alone
for forcing selection. Projections provide a terminal plausibility overlay.

## Invoking one workflow

```bash
pixi shell
snakemake all -c 3 -s build_model.smk --configfile test_case/project_config_rapid.yml
```

The flags worth knowing:

| Flag | Effect |
|---|---|
| `-s` | which workflow file to run |
| `--configfile` | the YAML configuration |
| `-c` | cores; more than 1 enables parallelism |
| `--dry-run`, `-n` | list what would execute, run nothing |
| `--unlock` | clear the working-directory lock left by a crash |
| `--keep-going`, `-k` | keep running independent jobs after a failure |
| `--notemp` | keep intermediate files Snakemake would delete |

The full option set is in the [Snakemake CLI
documentation](https://snakemake.readthedocs.io/en/stable/executing/cli.html).

The recommended sequence for any workflow is: render the graph, clear a stale
lock if there is one, then run.

```bash
python scripts/plot_workflow_dag.py -s build_model.smk --configfile <config>
snakemake --unlock -s build_model.smk --configfile <config>
snakemake all -c 3 -s build_model.smk --configfile <config>
```

The first command renders a DAG image into `<project_dir>/logs/dag/`, named
after the run that would produce it (`<project_name>_wf<N>_dag.png`, with the
stress test carrying its experiment id). It draws the graph and runs nothing;
it needs Graphviz's `dot`, which the pixi environment provides.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Dry-run after editing anything structural

`--dry-run` validates the whole dependency graph in seconds. Run it after
changing a rule, a script signature, or any config key that feeds a rule's
inputs — it is the difference between finding a broken path now and finding it
forty minutes into a model build.
:::

## CPU and memory budgets

WF4's Julia jobs reserve `runtime.julia_threads` (default 4) within Snakemake's
total `--cores` budget. The actual allocation is passed to Julia. With `-c 3`,
one Julia batch runs with three threads; `-c 12` permits up to three four-thread
batches. This replaces the previous behavior where `-c 3` could launch three
four-thread Julia processes. Choose a budget that fits the machine and other work.

The main WF2 analysis jobs and WF4 indicator reduction reserve 1024 MB each;
weather generation, perturbation, downscaling and Wflow reserve 2048 MB each.
These are initial scheduling reservations, **not measured peak-memory guarantees**
or process limits. Set the total budget and override reservations using observed
peak RSS from the workflow benchmarks, especially for larger basins:

```bash
python scripts/simulate_system.py --config test_case/project_config_rapid.yml --target all --cores 12 -- --resources mem_mb=8192 --set-resources downscale_climate_realization:mem_mb=4096
```

Without `--resources mem_mb=...`, the declarations do not impose a total RAM
budget. Resource overrides also belong in a Snakemake execution profile; they do
not belong in the scientific project configuration. Batched Wflow rule names are
`run_wflow_batch_<number>`; `--set-threads` overrides for them are included
conservatively when estimating batch concurrency and temporary disk use.

WF2 computes change-factor summaries in memory and reuses historical statistics
within the job. WF4 computes PET in HydroMT during downscaling, reads each
simulation CSV once for all indicators, and writes no unused per-member final
state. Input-state settings are preserved; WF1 still retains its final state.

## Running everything the config enables

`scripts/run_workflows.py` reads the `workflows.<name>.enabled` flags and runs
Snakemake for exactly the enabled workflows, in order:

```bash
pixi run run-workflows --config test_case/project_config_rapid.yml
pixi run run-workflows --config <config> --cores 4 -- --dry-run
```

What it guarantees:

- It accepts **full-orchestration configs only** — a `workflows:` section with
  all five subsections, each with an `enabled:` key.
- A missing section or key is a **hard error naming the absent key**, never a
  silent default.
- It **stops at the first nonzero Snakemake exit and returns that code**, so a
  failed upstream workflow is never followed by a downstream run.
- `--cores N`, and anything after a `--` sentinel, forwards to every invocation.
- Every invocation — including a dry run, a no-op, or a failure — writes an
  immutable manifest under `<project_dir>/config/runs/invocations/`.

It narrates its own run: which project, which config, a numbered sequence of the
enabled workflows, a line at each workflow's start and finish with its duration,
and a closing verdict listing what was written. Every line it speaks is bounded
by a full-width rule that nothing else in the console draws, so you can always
tell the runner's voice from the workflow's.

::: {.callout-note}
## Run the pipeline from one checkout

Snakemake keeps its "what is up to date" bookkeeping in a `.snakemake/`
directory under the *working directory*, and it locks that directory while
running. Driving one `project_dir` from two checkouts gives you two
disagreeing sets of bookkeeping and two independent locks over the same output
files. Pick one checkout for runs and stay in it.
:::

## Retained metrics and model rebuilds

An experiment freezes its collection, model and simulator settings. Changed
simulation inputs require a new `experiment_name`; deleting a model-reference
file does not authorize replacing the frozen simulation identity.

For new metrics from existing responses, set `operation: metrics-only` and keep
the experiment name in the simulation settings file:

```bash
python scripts/simulate_system.py --config <config> --target metrics --cores 3
```

This operation uses retained response and simulation records; it needs no live
model, generation inputs or Julia. The all-workflow runner accepts
`--simulation-target metrics`; disable other stages for a retained-only run.
The default `all` target does not infer an operation from existing files.
See [retained handoffs](../wf3-retained-handoffs.md).
